title: Degree of an Array
summary: Given a non-empty array of non-negative integers, determine the smallest length of a contiguous subarray that matches the degree of the original array.
statement: Given a non-empty array of non-negative integers, determine the smallest length of a contiguous subarray that matches the degree of the original array. The degree of an array is the highest frequency of any single element within it.
constraints: Return the shortest contiguous subarray with the same maximum frequency (degree) as the full array.
hints: For a chosen value, the shortest subarray containing all its occurrences spans its first through last occurrence.
Track first index, running count, current degree, and best span online.
On a new degree replace the answer; on an equal degree minimize with index-first[value]+1.
Any subarray retaining the full degree must include every occurrence of at least one degree-achieving value.
editorial: Any subarray retaining the full degree must include every occurrence of at least one degree-achieving value.

tests.explanation: The array degree is two, and [2,2] is the shortest matching subarray.
Two appears three times, spanning indices one through six for length six.
